questions.question: Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal empire from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is from __**1658 to 1707 AD**__.

__
 
• **Aurangzeb ruled the Mughal empire from 1658 to 1707 AD**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aurangzeb (1658 AD-1707 AD):**

 
 
• Aurangzeb defeated Dara at Dharmat (1658 AD), Samugarh (1658 AD), and Deorai, in which Samugarh was the decisive one and Deorai was the last one.
 
• After the victory, Aurangzeb was crowned at Delhi under the title ***Alamgir***. He **died in February 1707 **in **Ahmadnagar**.
 
• Aurangzeb captured **Guru Teg Bahadur**, the 9th Guru of Sikhs in 1675 AD and executed him when he refused to embrace Islam.
 
 
• The **10th and last Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh**, son of Guru Teg Bahadur, organized his followers into a community of warriors called ***Khalsa*** to fight against the Muslims.
 
 
 
• **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj** was the most powerful Maratha king and an arch-enemy of Aurangzeb.
 
• The Mughal conquests reached a climax during Aurangzeb’s reign as **Bijapur **and **Golconda **were annexed in **1686 AD and 1687 AD**, respectively.
 
• Under him, the Mughal empire reached its greatest extent and the largest single-state ever known in India.
 
• He forbade the inscription of ***Kalma ***on the coins, also forbade **sati and Jharokha-darshan**.
 
• He** ended the celebration of Navroz** and, in 1679 AD, **reimposed Jizya. **
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Aurangzeb was initiated into the** Naqshbandiya order.**
 
• The only monument associated with Aurangzeb is ***Bibi ka Maqbara***, which is the tomb of his wife **Rabbia-ud-Daura, in Aurangabad.**

questions.question: Moti Masjid in Agra fort was constructed by which of the following Mughal Emperors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shahjahan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shahjahan:**

 
 
• Shahjahan reigned during the peak of Mughal architectural splendor.
 
• He commissioned the Moti Masjid (Pearl Mosque) within the Agra Fort, known for its pristine white marble construction.
 
• His most iconic creation is the Taj Mahal, a testament to his love for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He also significantly redesigned the Agra Fort, adding numerous marble structures.
 
• Shahjahan built the Jama Masjid in Delhi, another architectural masterpiece.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aurangzeb:**

 
 
• Aurangzeb's reign saw a decline in Mughal architectural patronage.
 
• While he did construct the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore, his focus shifted more towards military campaigns and expanding the empire.
 
• His architectural style was less ornate than that of Shah Jahan.
 
• Aurangzeb's rule is often characterized by its strict adherence to Islamic law.
 
• His rule expanded the Mughal empires territory to its largest size.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir:**
 
 
• Jahangir was known for his love of art and gardens.
 
• He continued the construction of Akbar's tomb in Sikandra.
 
• He significantly contributed to the development of Mughal painting.
 
• Jahangir also designed many beautiful gardens.
 
• His rule was known for relative peace, and prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• Akbar's architectural style blended Persian and Indian influences.
 
• He built the Agra Fort, although Shahjahan later modified it extensively.
 
• He also constructed the city of Fatehpur Sikri, including the Buland Darwaza and Panch Mahal.
 
• He was known for his religious tolerance.
 
• Akbar's rule consolidated the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: Babur introduced a technique of warfare called '____' which divided the army into different divisions to flank the enemy from all sides.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tulughma**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The new war tactics introduced by Babur were the** tulughma and the araba.**
 
• Tulughma meant dividing the whole army into various units, viz. the **Left, the Right and the Centre.**
 
• The Left and Right divisions were further subdivided into Forward and Rear divisions.
 
• Through this a small army could be used to surround the **enemy from all the sides.**
 
• The Centre Forward division was then provided with carts (araba) which were placed in rows facing the enemy and tied to each other with animal hide ropes.
 
• Behind them were placed cannons protected and supported by **mantelets **which could be used to **easily manoeuvre the canons. **
 
• These two tactics made** Babur’s artillery lethal.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• The First Battle of Panipat (21 April 1526) fought near a small village of Panipat Haryana.
 
• The battle was fought between the invading forces of Zahir-ud-din Babur and Lodi Empire during the rule of Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• The Mughal forces of Babur, the ruler of Kabulistan, defeated ruling army of Ibrahim Lodi, Sultan of Delhi.
 
• Babur’s tactics of *Tulughma and Araba *__that led him to victory.

questions.question: The construction of Humayun's tomb was completed by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biga Begum**__.

__
 
• The construction of **Humayun's Tomb** was commissioned by his widow, **Biga Begum**, also known as **Haji Begum**.
 
• It was built in memory of the Mughal Emperor **Humayun** and is considered the first significant example of **Mughal architecture** in India.
 
• The tomb was designed by the Persian architect **Mirak Mirza Ghiyas**, reflecting the **Persian style of architecture** with Indian influences.
 
• The construction was completed in the year **1571**, about 15 years after Humayun's death in **1556**.
 
• It is located in **Delhi, India**, and is a UNESCO **World Heritage Site**.
 
• The complex is known for its **charbagh (four-part) garden layout**, which became a hallmark of Mughal gardens.
 
• **Red sandstone and white marble** were extensively used in its construction, showcasing the grandeur of the Mughal era.
 
• The structure served as inspiration for later Mughal monuments, including the **Taj Mahal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• **Zeenat Mahal** was the wife of the last Mughal Emperor **Bahadur Shah Zafar**.
 
• She was known for her influence in the Mughal court during the declining years of the empire.
 
• She had no connection with the construction of **Humayun's Tomb**.
 
 
 
• **Mah Chuchak Begum**__
 __
 
• **Mah Chuchak Begum** was a wife of **Humayun** and played a political role during the Mughal reign.
 
• She was known for her governance in **Kabul** after Humayun's death.
 
• However, she was not involved in the construction of **Humayun's Tomb**.

• There is no historical evidence of her involvement in the construction of the tomb.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements in the context of the Mughal Rule.

1. The Mansabdari System was introduced by Akbar in 1571.

2. The Second Battle of Panipat was fought in 1556.

3. Maharana Pratap Singh of Mewar was a contemporary of Babur.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari System** was introduced by **Akbar** in **1571**. It was a unique administrative system for grading officials and assigning them ranks (mansabs) based on their performance and responsibilities. This system helped in centralizing the administration and maintaining a strong military.
 
• The **Second Battle of Panipat** was fought in **1556** between the forces of the Mughal emperor Akbar, led by Bairam Khan, and the local king Hemu. This battle marked the consolidation of Mughal power in India under Akbar's rule.
 
• **Maharana Pratap Singh** of Mewar was not a contemporary of Babur but of Akbar. Babur ruled during the early 16th century, while Maharana Pratap was a 16th-century ruler who fiercely resisted Akbar's expansionist policies.
 
• The Mansabdari system and the Second Battle of Panipat are crucial milestones in Indian history as they laid the foundation for Akbar's administrative and military success.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mansabdari System**__

 __
 
• The Mansabdari system was based on the numerical rank assigned to officers, which determined their status and salary.
 
• Ranks were divided into **Zat** (personal rank) and **Sawar** (number of cavalry maintained).
 
• This system was crucial in organizing the Mughal military and administration effectively.
 
• It ensured loyalty among the officers and allowed Akbar to maintain a strong and centralized empire.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Panipat**__
 __
 
• This battle was significant in establishing Mughal dominance in northern India.
 
• **Hemu**, the local king, was defeated by Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent, despite putting up a strong resistance.
 
• The victory solidified Akbar's position as the ruler and marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire's golden era.
 
 
 
• **Maharana Pratap Singh**__
 
 
• Maharana Pratap was a ruler of **Mewar**, and he is remembered for his bravery and resistance against Akbar's invasions.
 
• He fought the famous **Battle of Haldighati** against Akbar's forces led by Man Singh in 1576.
 
• Maharana Pratap is considered a symbol of Rajput pride and independence.

questions.question: On the maternal side, the Mughals were descendants of ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genghis Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On the **maternal side**, the Mughals were descendants of **Genghis Khan**.
 
• **Genghis Khan**, originally named **Temujin**, was the founder of the **Mongol Empire**, which became the largest contiguous empire in history.
 
• He was born in the year **1162** and established the Mongol Empire by uniting the **nomadic tribes** of Northeast Asia.
 
• The Mughal dynasty in India traced its lineage to him through their founder, **Babur**, whose mother was a descendant of Genghis Khan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tajuddin Yalduz**__

 __
 
• **Tajuddin Yalduz** was a ruler of the **Ghurid Empire** in the 13th century.
 
• He was not directly related to the Mughal lineage.
 
 
 
• **Timur**__
 __
 
• **Timur**, also known as **Tamerlane**, was a 14th-century conqueror and the founder of the **Timurid Empire** in Persia and Central Asia.
 
• On the paternal side, the Mughals were descendants of Timur.

• Although Humayun initiated its construction, Sher Shah Suri contributed several structures to the fort. Dating back to the** 16th century, **the Purana Quila stands as one of Delhi's oldest forts.
 
• Functioning as the inner citadel of the **city of Dinpanah**, the fort is positioned near the Pragati Maidan exhibition ground. Its walls, towering at 18 meters in height, extend over a length of 1 to 5 kilometers.
 
• Throughout its history, the Purana Quila has borne witness to the rise and fall of empires and the reign of mighty rulers.
 
• Sher Shah Suri is credited with the creation of several interior structures within the fort, notably the **Qila-i-Kuhn mosque and the Sher Mandal.**
 
• These architectural elements add to the historical significance and grandeur of the Purana Quila.

• **Nasir al-Din Muhammad,** known by his regnal name Humayun, served as the second Mughal emperor, reigning over territories encompassing present-day Eastern Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Northern India, and Pakistan.
 
• His rule extended from 1530 to 1540 and was interrupted, only to be restored from 1555 until his passing in 1556. By the time of his death, the Mughal Empire had expanded to cover nearly one million square kilometers.
 
• **Sher Shah Suri,** often hailed as the "Just King," emerged as the founder of the Sur Empire in India. Initially serving as regent and later assuming sole rulership of Bihar from 1529 to 1540, he rose to prominence by defeating the Mughal Empire in 1540. T
 
• his victory led to the establishment of the Sur Empire, with Delhi as its capital, and Sher Shah Suri declaring himself Emperor. Following his accidental demise in 1545 CE, his son, Islam Shah, succeeded him as ruler.

• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire in India, was a follower of the **Naqshbandi Sufi order**.
 
• The Naqshbandi order is one of the major Sunni spiritual orders of Sufism.
 
• It emphasizes the inner relationship between the seeker and God, focusing on silent meditation (zikr).
 
• Babur's connection with the Naqshbandi order influenced his personal and political life, including his tolerant religious policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Sufism is the mystical Islamic belief and practice in which Muslims seek the truth of divine love and knowledge through direct personal experience of God.
 
• Sufi orders are often referred to as "Silsilas," which means chain or lineage, representing the chain of spiritual masters going back to Prophet Muhammad.
 
 
 
• **Naqshbandi Order**
 
 
• The Naqshbandi order was founded by Baha-ud-Din Naqshband Bukhari in the 14th century.
 
• It is known for its silent meditation and the emphasis on the heart's connection with God rather than vocal chanting.
 
 
 
• **Babur**
 
 
• Babur (1483-1530) was the first Mughal emperor of India, establishing the Mughal dynasty which ruled for over 300 years.
 
• He wrote a famous autobiography, the Baburnama, which provides insights into his life and the early Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Religious Tolerance**
 
 
• Babur's association with Sufism, particularly the Naqshbandi order, influenced his approach to governance, including his policies of religious tolerance.
 
• This legacy of tolerance was carried forward by his descendants, notably Akbar the Great.

questions.question: What were cash crops such as cotton and sugarcane called during the Mughal period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jins-i-kamil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the Mughal Period, the land was divided into four categories namely
 
 
• Polaj - Which was cultivated every year.
 
• Parati - Which was sometimes left uncultivated for one or two years.
 
• Chachar - Which was left uncultivated for three or four years.
 
• Banjar - Which was left uncultivated for five years or more.
 
 
 
• Polaj was the land that is annually cultivated for each crop in succession and is never allowed to lie fallow.
 
• **Polaj** was the ideal and best type of** land throughout the empire.**
 
• This land was cultivated always and was **never allowed to lie fallow. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There was no **Mughal land revenue system **before **Akbar**.
 
• His father Humayun and grandfather Babur did not introduce any changes because they were the first conquerors of their dynasty and remained pre-occupied with subduing rebellions, consolidating empires, and maintaining order.
 
• A prope**r land revenue system **was founded by **Akbar**.
 
• However, the system of Akbar was itself based on what **Shershah Suri **implemented during his short tenure.
 
• Thus, the land revenue system of Akbar was neither innovation nor an invention.
 
• His indebtedness to the earlier rulers is immense but this has not diminished his fame as far as **the land revenue system **is concerned.
 
• He followed the policy of **Shershah** with greater precision and correctness and then extended it to various subah or provinces of his empire.
 
• But this correction or precision did not come overnight.
 
• Initially was tortuous enough to turn peasants into **beggars**, and forcing them to **sell their wives and children.**
 
• But it was revised several times.
 
• **The corrections done by the Akbar inland revenue system were as follows:**
 
 
• Standardization of measurement of land
 
• Ascertaining the produce per Bigha of Land
 
• Fixation of state’s share in that produce

questions.question: Which of the following customs of inheritance was followed by the Mughals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Coparcenary inheritance.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindu Succession Law-related issues** are referred to as coparcenary.
 
• It describes a person who, by** virtue of birth**, is capable of **assuming a legal right** to his **ancestors' property.**
 
• **"Unity of title, possession, and interest"** is what it signifies.
 
• The **coparcenary rule of inheritance**, which the Mughals followed, **split the entire empire **among all the sons.
 
• They did not adhere to the **primogeniture principle**, according to which the **father's property was given to the eldest son.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ancestral property:**

 
 
• Ancestral property is the possessions that a Hindu **inherits by birth from his or her father, father's father, or father's father's father.**
 
 
 
• **Rule of primogeniture:**
 
 
• The** firstborn legitimate child **of a deceased person receives their **inheritance** under the principle of primogeniture.
 
 
 
• **Self-acquired intestate:**
 
 
• A succession that occurs intestate is one that **does not have a will. **When a** person passes away **without leaving a will dictating who gets what, it's known as **dying intestate.**
